locations.name: Perimeter
locations.description:
Perimeter appears to be part of colony expansion and terraplatforming efforts.

Its data Wall, Hauler, and Twin Relays suggest heavy data collection and transmission, though the purpose and outcome remain unclear. 

Most systems read as dormant.

content.description: A mobile control unit supporting DATA WALL operations and local monitoring, used in planetary exploration and viable colony zone identification.
A runoff and filtration site in support of the zoneâs initial excavation and terraplatforming.
A secondary relay built to expand data volume; its derelict status suggests disrepair and accelerated entropy.
An operational hub that coordinated the zoneâs geological monitoring and resource collection efforts.
A massive communication and data relay that appears to be engineered to collate, condense, and transfer information collected by the zoneâs central data wall.
A mobile survey structure placed along a deliberate path to collect subsurface planetary readings and feed them into nearby systems when active.
The eastern section of the Data Wall is heavily damaged and no longer appears operational. Despite this, Runners frequently use the structure to move between Station and South Relay.

A network of maintenance tunnels appears to connect Station and the Data Wall, with additional outlets near Ravine and South Relay. Their full extent is unclear, but they are commonly used to move between regions out of sight.

The terrain suggests this area once served as a natural runoff path for wastewater from Station and the Data Wall toward Overflow. A small monitoring structure provides limited cover when crossing the open space between regions.
This area is defined by a dense cluster of tall rock formations. The narrow sightlines and uneven terrain make it difficult to read movement, and threats often emerge with little warning.

locations.name: Dire Marsh
locations.description:
Located in the colonyâs former farming sector. 

The zone contains research, cultivation, and processing facilities tied to food sustainability efforts. Environmental conditions are marshland with limited visibility and broad sightlines. Automated systems show signs of partial operation.

A quarantine operation was initiated here prior to abandonment. The presence of an unidentified anomaly intersects multiple regions of the zone.

content.description: Equipment and lab layouts indicate active study of Tau Ceti IV plant life for pharmaceutical applications. Safety infrastructure suggests highârisk experimentation.
The region features shallow growth pools and research stations that focus on protein alternatives using native organisms. Elevated structures provide clear views across adjacent areas.
An emergency contagion control site deployed to the zoneâs western edge to contain some level of unidentified threat using isolation units and outbreak protocols.
This maintenance facility supported the heavy equipment used to seed and harvest the growfields beyond the zone. Its structures appear intact but inactive.
When its systems were functional, AI UPLINK connected the local support intelligence to the wider colony network and the Marathon ship.
The region appears dedicated to seed development, controlled plant growth, and bio-manipulated produce. Systems are automated and remain partially active.

Appears to have served as the central command structure for this zoneâs agricultural operations. Upper levels are sealed. Groundâlevel access points and a landing pad indicate outbound transport activity at some point.
This monitoring station appears to have regulated water flow when Dire Marsh was active. Its placement suggests it played a role in maintaining reserves for seeding and harvesting operations.

This checkpoint was likely used to control all traffic entering and leaving Dire Marshâs core facilities. Structural differences suggest it may have been added later, possibly in response to security concerns.

An unidentified energy pattern has cut through Dire Marsh, leaving a visible distortion across the terrain. Its origin and behavior remain unknown, and its presence has drawn increasing attention from both Runners and the UESC.
This checkpoint is severely damaged and completely offline. When functional, it likely served as the primary exit for shipments moving out to other colony locations.
The West Gate appears to have functioned as the zoneâs primary entry checkpoint. Its layout suggests early screening and resource monitoring before materials were routed deeper into the zone.

locations.name: Outpost
locations.description:
Outposts were the tip-of-the-spear for Tau Ceti colonization efforts. 

This zoneâs layout points to staging and logistics for planetary expeditions: launch, intake, processing, housing. 

Everything that followed started here.

content.description: Sample intake and resourcing from planetary expeditions. Returning drones, rovers, and dropcraft passed through this region.
The pinwheel is Outpostâs central structure. Its three distinct wings are command, drone control, and fabrication, which has suffered significant damage.
Tight living blocks and interior corridors with limited exits. Reports of UESC activity here are frequent enough to take seriously.
This is where early colonists were welcomed to Tau Ceti IV. Its spaces were designed to brief and condition new arrivals, preparing them for life in an alien solar system.
Flight Control appears to have managed inbound and outbound traffic for Outpost operations. Records and layout suggest coordination of exploration flights and early planetary surveillance missions.
Landing and service for dropcraft and support vehicles. Facilities include loading deck, maintenance bay, and vertical landing slots for rapid deployment.
The Command Wing likely served as the operational center for Outpost leadership. Its proximity to other core facilities suggests coordination with both surface teams and command aboard the Marathon.
The Drone Wing was used to service and deploy planetary surveillance drones. Equipment placement indicates preparation, programming, and launch were all handled from this location.
This area is notable for its extensive damage. It is believed to have been the Outpostâs fabrication and maintenance facility, though the cause and timing of its destruction remain unclear.
